title: Drawing a C4 architecture diagram
purpose: Draws one view of a C4 model (a system context, container or component view) from JSON an agent writes: `render` lays it out and returns SVG, people on top and the scope's children inside a dashed boundary, and `mermaid` and `d2` write the same view as text for places that draw it themselves, such as a Mermaid block in Markdown on GitHub.
inputs: The model as JSON: `people`, `systems` with their `containers` and `components`, `relationships` and `views`, from a file in the workspace, stdin, or `--text`. Name the view with `--view` when there's more than one. `render --out <file>` writes the SVG to a new file instead.
examples: toil util c4 render bookshop.c4.json --view containers --out c4.svg
toil util c4 mermaid bookshop.c4.json --view context
toil util c4 d2 bookshop.c4.json --view components
verifies: The whole model is checked before anything is drawn, with every problem named by its path. `render` then checks its own drawing: no two boxes overlap, every child sits inside its boundary and nothing else does, every arrow starts and ends on its boxes, no arrow passes behind a box it doesn't join, and no label covers a box. The text renders check that every element is declared once and every arrow has its line. Layout runs in a worker thread with a deadline.
limits: Text is measured with Helvetica's widths, so a much wider substitute font can overflow a box. toil doesn't run Mermaid or D2, so whether their text draws is unchecked. A model holds at most 1,000 elements, 2,000 relationships and 100 views, and `render` draws at most 100 boxes and 250 arrows in one view. No PNG.
